newsitem.title: UK: Brown says UK must control inflation pressures.
newsitem.headline: Brown says UK must control inflation pressures.

text.p: Britain must bring inflation under control to avoid a return to the boom-and-bust cycle which has dogged it in the past, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Thursday.
His comments followed the central bank's decision to raise official interest rates by 25 basis points, taking them to 6.75 percent.

"Today the Bank of England has agreed with me that we must prevent a return to the cycle of boom-and-bust and that inflationary pressures in the economy which, despite persistent warnings, the previous government negligently failed to tackle, must be brought under control," Brown said in a statement.

"The budget set out a long-term framework for monetary and fiscal stability to achieve our objective of high and stable levels of growth and employment by taking tough action now to bring the deficit now and to bring inflation down.
"The government and the Bank of England are determined to ensure that this country does not return to the instability and negative equity of the 1980s and the early 1990s," Brown said.

Brown tightened fiscal policy by 5.5 billion stg in his budget, targeting most of the rise at the corporate sector. This increased market speculation that interest rates would have to go up to calm the rampant consumer sector.
